messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on sm86 w/ the new arch-prober + triton->cutlass fallback enabled. saw a regression on medium-length chat (>1024 tokens) after fp8 calibration landed. p99 doubled in some cases. :frowning:
Sam: ugh. any repro steps/flags? or a specific model/seq_len?
Maya: repro was on gpt-like-3b, seq 128/512/2048. flags: `--arch-prober=enabled --prefer-cutlass=auto --fp8-calib=on`
Maya: sample cmd:
```
./serve --model gpt-3b --device a100 --arch-prober=on --prefer-cutlass=auto --fp8-calib=on --max-batch-tokens=4096
```
Sam: can you paste a tiny perf snippet? numbers or flame output enough.
Maya: pasted raw qps/p99 from our internal run (local canary):
```
baseline (no-calib, prefer-cutlass=false): qps=420 p50=12ms p99=23ms
after fp8 calib + prober auto: qps=360 p50=14ms p99=48ms
```
Liam: interesting — p50 barely moved, p99 jumped. smells like occasional fallback / mutex / kv-cache cold misses. did you see any KV cache eviction logs? :eyes:
Maya: yeah saw a few `kv_align_fallback` logs and `cutlass_fallback: alignment mismatch` sprinkled at the same timestamps as the tail latency spikes.
Nina: could be our batching heuristic + kv prefetch not playing nice with the fp8 kernel alignment requirements. fp8 kernels require 128-byte aligned KV blocks on this build/arch, otherwise triton path falls back and we hit a slower codepath.
Sam: what's the build flag we set for alignment? `-DUSE_ALIGNED_KV=ON`? we toggled that a while ago for sm90.
Nina: build flag is `-DKV_ALIGN_ENFORCE=1` in the runtime build. but the arch-prober sets `prefer-cutlass` depending on `sm_version` and kernel availability. prober might be pessimistic and flip to a fallback path at runtime.
Liam: quick check — try forcing `--prefer-cutlass=false` and bump `--kv-cache-prefetch=16` on the canary. that avoids the triton kernels that require the strict alignment and should reduce fallback frequency.
Maya: tried that locally, qps improved but still saw intermittent spikes. Also noticed `max_batch_tokens` heuristic sometimes produces very wide batches with small seqs which aggravates kv hot-set thrashing.
Sam: maybe change batching heuristic to cap max sequences per batch when kv cache miss rate > X. we already have telemetry for `kv_miss_rate` per pod.
Maya: agreed. plan: 1) run canary disabling triton path (`--prefer-cutlass=false`) 2) temp change heuristic: `if kv_miss_rate > 0.02 => max_seq_in_batch = min(8, current)` 3) run with fp8-calib=off and on to isolate calibration cost.
perf-bot: Canary started on cluster-r1: canary-id=canary-1945209876-1, target=3 pods.
Liam: also try a build toggle test — rebuild runtime with `-DKV_ALIGN_ENFORCE=0 -DUSE_CUTLASS=ON` vs `-DUSE_CUTLASS=OFF` to see whether CUTLASS kernel itself has alignment handling. CUTLASS sometimes tolerates unaligned inputs via internal memcpy but triton kernels bail earlier.
Nina: good call. I suspect the triton->cutlass runtime handoff path has an extra memcpy that disables prefetch optimizations, causing latency tail.
Sam: can someone attach a small flame ASCII of the slow request? even stack frames help.
Maya: attached snippet from perf profiler (trimmed):
```
[01] runtime::dispatch_triton_kernel
[01] runtime::kv_cache_lookup (slow)
[01] runtime::cutlass_fallback (memcpy)
[01] kernel::fp8_quantize
[01] kernel::attention_kv
```
Liam: that shows memcpy in fallback path — confirms extra copy. question: is memcpy happening because prober marks kernel as incompatible or because the buffer isn't 128B aligned?
Maya: logs indicate `alignment=64` for the buffer at fault. config shows our allocator uses 64B by default for that workload.
Nina: allocator tweak idea: add allocation hint for KV buffers when `fp8_enabled` to enforce 128B alignment at alloc time. cheap fix, no kernel changes.
Sam: sounds low-risk. who can spin that change?
Nina: I can add a runtime allocator flag `kv_align_hint=128` behind a feature flag for the canary. I'll also add a telemetry ping when allocator gives a 128 vs 64 alignment.
Maya: excellent. after that I'd like to re-run with `--fp8-calib=on` and `prefer-cutlass=auto` to see if tail goes away.
perf-bot: Canary update: canary-1945209876-1 replica-2 reported p99=26ms after allocator hint applied (prelim), kv_miss_rate=0.015.
Liam: promising. follow-ups: 1) roll allocator hint to canary cluster-wide, 2) test build variations for CUTLASS vs TRITON fallback cost, 3) consider prober heuristics: prefer-cutlass only when allocator alignment >=128 or when kv_miss_rate < threshold.
Maya: I'll open a short RFC with proposed heuristics and canary data. tagging for follow-up: @Sam @Nina @Liam. :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks — will help with the build matrix tests.
Nina: I'll push the allocator flag PR to canary branch.
Maya: closing the loop once we have full canary data. thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
